studies.label: Within-subject laboratory experiment on scientific divergent applications
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Section 3.1 (PDF p. 15) reports a Subject ID random effect. No separate adjustment for two-person teams is stated; the number of teams and the allocation of condition-order sequences are not printed.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 7, Section 2.1 Participants; all participants completed every condition, PDF p. 8, Section 2.2
counts_source.quote: A total of 100 participants were recruited via an online questionnaire. Four participants were excluded for failing to follow task instructions, resulting in a final sample of 96

arms.name: Group-AI (G-AI)
arms.description: Two-person team exchanges ideas in a public QQ chat panel, taking turns. Each member has their own ChatGPT-4o and may ask one task-related question during their own turn.

arms.name: Individual-AI (I-AI)
arms.description: Participant works one-on-one with ChatGPT-4o, entering ideas in a private panel that shows only their own input.

arms.name: Human-only group (G)
arms.description: Two-person team exchanges ideas by turns in the public chat panel; the AI interface is disabled. The human partner supplies the non-AI aid.

studies.task: Generate novel applications of transparent ceramics, electronic skin, and crystal resin in the scientific divergent application task, with different materials used across the counterbalanced collaboration conditions.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4o (OpenAI)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 8, Section 2.2 Procedure: The AI system used was ChatGPT-4o, developed by OpenAI. A model release year is not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration statement or link was found in the saved PDF. PDF p. 7, Section 2.1, reports an a priori power analysis.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Realistic applicability of the produced ideas, rated by ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek on a 5-point scale (1 = not at all useful, 5 = very useful). The paper does not state how scores from ideas or raters were aggregated for each condition.

regression.model: Mixed-effects model: collaboration condition fixed effect; Subject ID random effect. The covariates used in this specific model are not stated.

sources.quote: A total of 100 participants were recruited via an online questionnaire. Four participants were excluded for failing to follow task instructions, resulting in a final sample of 96
Each participant completed three experimental conditions.
creative usefulness (the extent to which the ideas could be realistically applied, rated on a 5-point Likert scale; 1 = not at all useful, 5 = very useful)
we assessed creative usefulness and originality in the current study using two AI systems, namely ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek.
participants in the group-AI condition reported higher usefulness scores (M = 4.09, SD = 0.35)
human-only group (M = 3.24, SD = 0.31)
usefulness scores in the group-AI condition were significantly higher than in the human-only group condition (β = 0.84, SE = 0.04, p < 0.001)
Subject ID was entered as a random effect to account for individual variability, while collaboration condition was treated as a fixed effect.

estimates.notes: This is the full-sample within-person comparison; no first-round result is printed. The n fields count the same analyzed people in both conditions and once in n_total, using the final sample and the statement that everyone completed every condition. They do not establish independent outcome rows. Score aggregation and the level of the printed SDs are unconfirmed, so unit, n_units, and sd_level are null. The printed β is retained as a mixed-model coefficient on the reported outcome scale; no standardized outcome is described, and it is not coded as a standardized effect. se_basis is participant because the paper explicitly reports a Subject ID random effect; adequate adjustment for dependence between teammates is not established. The baseline controls named in Section 2.3 are not explicitly listed in the Section 3.1 model.

open_items: The paper does not state whether the condition means and SDs summarize people, teams, outputs, or ratings; nor does it explain how partners, ideas, and the two model judges were aggregated. unit, n_units, and sd_level are null.

Section 3.1 reports a Subject ID random effect, which is coded as participant SE basis under the extraction specification. Whether this also accounts adequately for dependence between teammates is unresolved; no team-level adjustment or model observation count is printed.

The analyzed sample is printed only for the experiment as a whole. The retained people counts describe that complete within-person sample, not independent outcome observations; outcome-specific inclusion and model sample sizes are not separately reported.
Counts at random assignment, the exact condition-order randomization method, the stage at which exclusions were applied, and handling of excluded participants’ partners are not reported.
First-round outcome results, the within-person outcome correlations, and SDs of paired differences are not printed. No first-round effect or paired standardized effect was derived.

For ordinary fluency no arm means, SDs, contrast coefficient, SE, test statistic, or p-value is printed. For Individual-AI versus Human-only group, the other outcomes give only arm descriptives and a p-value bound.
The covariates in the creativity mixed-effects models, the precise ChatGPT-4o deployment/version, its release year, and the DeepSeek judge version are not specified.

The paper refers to Supplementary Figure 2A/2B, but no separate supplement is on file; main-text Figure 2 displays the named classification schemes. Changes in the later journal version remain unchecked.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. The complete markdown conversion, including references, was read; the saved PDF was inspected with pymupdf, and all six figure images were viewed in memory. There are no tables or appendices in this PDF; it ends with references on PDF pp. 28-31. Page locators are PDF file pages; the manuscript has no printed page numbers. Source quotes retain printed numerical precision and normalize whitespace only. The final sample and every arm contain the same analyzed people, as confirmed by PDF pp. 7-8; the recruited count was not substituted for the unreported randomized count. Population is university students (PDF p. 1), and recruitment in China is stated on PDF pp. 26-27. Assignment is supported by random team assignment on PDF p. 7, counterbalancing on PDF p. 8, and Random Presentation in Figure 1B on PDF p. 9. The human-only arm is other_aid because of its human partner; adding AI to the same pair setup is ai_vs_bau, whereas individual AI versus the human pair is ai_vs_active. Group-AI versus Individual-AI also changes human partnership and the turn-taking constraints. All four creativity outcomes are called primary in Section 3.1, but no preregistration is stated. There is no overall creativity composite, across-people diversity result, or separate after-AI analysis. Only the main mixed-effects contrasts and their arm descriptives are extracted. PROCESS mediation results, including total-effect paths available only in Figures 5-6, are excluded under extraction Rules 1 and 5; no number was estimated from a plotted figure. Model rater-agreement statistics and random-effect variance components describe measurement/model structure and were not treated as arm contrasts. No effect, standard error, sample size, or SD was calculated from other statistics.
